0:00 / 0:00

A method, one step at a time

The film walks through the standard recipe of microbial experimental evolution: start from one clone, define the environment, propagate by serial transfer with a large bottleneck, freeze samples, replicate, and measure fitness by competition. For each step it shows what is done, why it is done, and what goes wrong without it.

It then follows the barcoding method of Levy et al. (2015), which tags each of about 500,000 yeast lineages with a random 20-letter DNA sequence so the whole race can be counted, and Kinsler, Geiler-Samerotte & Petrov (2020), who used the same barcodes to measure 292 adaptive mutants in 45 environments.
